security: For Manufacturing Data Engine, implement site connectivity, device/workload identity, tenant separation and sensitive operational-data controls.
Separate administrators, automation and runtime principals for asset hierarchy, telemetry stream, operational event and contextual model.
Audit Manufacturing Data Engine configuration and data access; protect its secrets, encryption keys and network paths according to workload classification.
operations: Monitor ingestion freshness, asset mapping quality, missing telemetry and pipeline availability for Manufacturing Data Engine.
Version sites/sources, asset model, ingestion endpoints, mappings, retention and analytics integration, test representative load/failure and retain a rollback or recovery path.
Assign explicit Manufacturing Data Engine ownership for quotas, maintenance, regional failure, dependency health and incident response.
watchPoints: OT connectivity and semantic mapping are customer responsibilities; raw signals without context do not create usable insights
Verify Manufacturing Data Engine regional availability, quotas, limits and compatibility before standardizing.
Manufacturing Data Engine's managed control plane does not remove schema, idempotency, data-quality or application-resilience responsibilities.
cost: connectivity, ingestion, storage, analytics and solution components.
Add dependent storage, network, logging and consuming/producing services to the Manufacturing Data Engine estimate.
Measure Manufacturing Data Engine cost per useful job, transaction, query or delivered workload rather than resource count alone.
alternatives: Manufacturing Data Engine — A manufacturing data foundation for contextualizing plant telemetry, assets and operational events for analytics and AI.
custom Pub/Sub/Dataflow/BigQuery platform when full bespoke control is required — use when its stated design fit dominates.

services.summary: A global asynchronous messaging service for topics, subscriptions, push/pull delivery, schemas and streaming ingestion.
concepts: topic, subscription, message, schema, snapshot and dead-letter topic define the Pub/Sub resource and data model.
The production path is publisher > topic > retained message > subscription > subscriber acknowledgment.
Pub/Sub manages its service control plane; workload correctness, data classification and downstream behavior remain architecture responsibilities.
applicationFit: Choose Pub/Sub when a global asynchronous messaging service for topics, subscriptions, push/pull delivery, schemas and streaming ingestion.
The strongest fit is a workload whose flow follows publisher > topic > retained message > subscription > subscriber acknowledgment.
Choose Cloud Tasks for per-item HTTP dispatch, scheduling and rate control instead when that alternative's operating model is the primary requirement.
